views.title: Expert judgment steers the work; agents carry it out.
views.claim: Thinking, Making and Sharing run in a loop, each ending at a point where a person decides. Knowledge, governance and execution sit underneath all three.
views.basis: Conceptual organisation of a personal working method. The three stages are the grouping used in the system's own documentation; the boxes underneath are surfaces, not a deployment diagram.
views.not_claimed: Not a company product, not an enterprise deployment, and not a runtime call graph.

views.title: Intent becomes a decision before anything is built.
views.claim: Research and tradeoff work are delegated to agents; the decision itself is not.
views.basis: Describes how discovery and shaping are done in practice. Which research and interview methods run depends on the question.
views.not_claimed: Does not claim every question follows every step, or that agents ever close a decision.

views.title: A decision becomes verified work through a governed path.
views.claim: A written specification is sliced, admitted by fixed rules, built by executors and checked by someone other than the builder.
views.basis: Matches the current build-and-verify workflow as documented in the working repository. Which tasks run in parallel follows their dependencies. Execution details are in the governed execution view.
views.not_claimed: Does not claim parallel execution for every task, or that review always passes the first time.

views.title: Work only counts once someone else can use it.
views.claim: The artifact is chosen for its reader, tested on a reader with no context, and released only with explicit approval.
views.basis: Describes the working practice for writing and publishing. The reader review is a separate pass by design, run on request or before publishing.
views.not_claimed: Does not claim every artifact gets every review, or that sending can ever happen without approval.

views.title: Autonomous work is admitted by rules, not by confidence.
views.claim: Shaping, certifying, admitting, building, reviewing and closing are separate roles with separate gates, and only a person closes work.
views.basis: Follows the current lifecycle and supervisor design; older orchestration designs that were retired are not shown. State names are generalised. Promotion to ready is a gated step an agent or a person can take; the supervisor then admits, never closes.
views.not_claimed: Not an audited runtime. The diagram shows the intended transitions and who may perform them. Not claimed: that the supervisor is the only route to review, or that it re-runs the tests itself.

views.title: Autonomy ends where an action is outward-facing or hard to undo.
views.claim: Reversible local work goes ahead. Anything outward-facing or hard to undo is drafted, held and approved one item at a time.
views.basis: Reflects the standing authorization policy for agent work. The list of reserved actions is representative, not exhaustive.
views.not_claimed: Does not claim every decision is automated, or that a hook catches every violation.

views.title: Context carries forward as records, not memory.
views.claim: Decisions, hypotheses and work records are kept separately, so a stranger could resume the work and a lesson earns its way into a rule.
views.basis: Describes the record types and their intended flow. Thresholds and automatic effects are summarised, not specified. Commits and decisions are captured by hooks; counting a hypothesis and promoting it happens at close-out, by an agent.
views.not_claimed: Does not claim the capture hooks fire in every repository.
